newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S PARLIAMENT REJECTS EXTRAORDINARY MEETING.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S PARLIAMENT REJECTS EXTRAORDINARY MEETING.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament, forced to assemble by storming protesters, on Friday postponed holding an extraordinary session to approve a "salvation declaration", which calls for early parliamentary elections.

Parliament, in which the ruling Socialists have a majority, voted against holding an extraordinary session by 89 for, 46 against and 58 abstained. The assembly halls are full of teargas as riot police tried to stave off opposition supporters who broke into the building earlier.
Parliament speaker Blagovest Sendov is holding a meeting with heads of parliamentary groups to discuss the situation.

Dozens of riot police clashed with as many demonstrators inside the building and tried to disperse them with hoses and tear gas. It also used teargas to try to disperse hundreds of opposition supporters who formed a human chain around parliament.
UDF deputies had walked out of parliament after the ruling Socialists rejected the vote on the "salvation declaration" earlier on Friday.
The opposition says the Bulgarian Socialist Party has failed to tackle the country's economic crisis and now lacks support to form a government.
